The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria has set December 2026 as the deadline for schools to ensure that at least 75 per cent of their teachers are professionally certified and licensed. Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, Dr Ronke Soyombo, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Abuja on Sunday. She said the measure was aimed at strengthening compliance with professional teaching standards. Soyombo said schools would be required to meet the certification threshold to qualify to apply for the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) and National Examinations Council (NECO) examinations. “By December 2026, schools will be required to have at least 75 per cent of their teachers certified and licensed by TRCN to qualify to apply for WAEC and NECO examinations,” she said. Soyombo said the council had integrated its website with WAEC and NECO through an Application Programming Interface (API) to enable the examination bodies to verify teachers’ professional status. The registrar said TRCN had commenced compliance monitoring, adding that it was engaging private school owners and administrators to encourage teachers to register for professional examinations and licensing. She, however, expressed concern over the low level of compliance, noting that many teachers had passed the professional qualifying examination but failed to complete the licensing process. “Our position is that every practising teacher must be professionally licensed. Soyombo said the council was also implementing an Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway to enable teachers without professional teaching qualifications to acquire the necessary training. She disclosed that during a recent teacher recruitment exercise in Nasarawa State, TRCN personnel discovered that 250 applicants had presented fake certificates out of approximately 1,000 applicants. She advised school owners to verify certificates presented by prospective employees, explaining that TRCN certificates carried QR codes that could be scanned to confirm their authenticity. The registrar added that the council was taking action against impersonation and certificate fraud, disclosing that a suspect identified as Godfrey had been remanded in prison. On improving service delivery, Soyombo said TRCN had established a six-member call centre to receive and address teachers’ complaints relating to registration, examinations and certification around the clock. She said the council had also decentralised its operations into geographical regions, with designated personnel responsible for attending to complaints and ensuring quicker responses. Soyombo explained that a monitoring system had been introduced to track applications awaiting verification, enabling her to identify delays and hold responsible officers accountable. She said the council was also providing step-by-step assistance to applicants experiencing difficulties with digital processes, adding that incorrect or incomplete academic documents often delayed verification. The registrar said the reforms were designed to strengthen accountability, eliminate fraudulent practices, improve professional standards and ensure that only qualified and licensed teachers practised in Nigerian schools.
